title: Eye injection (intravitreal injection)
what: The doctor injects medicine into the eye with a very fine needle. The eye is numbed with drops first.
why: For some retina conditions, such as age-related macular degeneration or retina changes from diabetes.
duration: the injection itself takes a few seconds, the whole visit usually 20 to 40 minutes; often a course of injections is needed
tell_doctor: Redness, discharge, or inflammation of the eye or eyelids
Allergy to iodine or eye drops
A recent heart attack or stroke

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your regular medicines on your own. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Makeup
prepare.text: Come without eye or face makeup.

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: You cannot drive after the injection. Come with someone.

steps: The eye is numbed with drops
The skin around the eye and the eye are cleaned with antiseptic
A small clip holds your eyelids open so you do not blink
You are asked to look to the side
The doctor gives the injection. It takes a few seconds
The eye is cleaned again, and vision and pressure are checked
feel: You feel pressure, but usually no pain
Afterward, a gritty feeling, sometimes spots or bubbles in your vision
after: Do not rub your eye or get it wet in the first days, as your doctor says
A small red spot on the white of the eye usually goes away on its own in 1 to 2 weeks
Use eye drops after the injection as prescribed
Come for your next injections on schedule
red_flags: Pain or redness gets worse, or vision drops sharply in the first days: see an eye doctor urgently
Pus coming from the eye: see an eye doctor urgently

faq.a: Usually not. The eye is numbed, and the injection takes seconds.

faq.q: How many injections will I need?
faq.a: Often a course, then maintenance injections. Your doctor will set the schedule.
You usually see only a blurry spot. You need to look to the side.

reminders.text: Eye injection tomorrow. Come without makeup and with someone. You cannot drive afterward.
